optionA: Encourage constructive discussions while ensuring they remain respectful, focused and aligned with project objectives.
optionB: Require only one team member to make all future technical decisions.
optionC: Separate the team members so they no longer work together.
optionD: Prevent disagreements by requiring every design decision to be approved by the sponsor.
explanation: Constructive conflict can improve creativity and decision quality when it remains professional and focused on project objectives. The project manager should facilitate healthy discussions rather than eliminate productive debate.

question: Which document defines how project costs will be planned, structured and controlled throughout the project?
optionA: Cost Management Plan
optionB: Project Charter
optionC: Cost Baseline
optionD: Business Case
explanation: The Cost Management Plan describes how project costs will be estimated, budgeted, managed, monitored and controlled. It establishes the processes used for cost management throughout the project lifecycle.

question: A project manager notices that a highly skilled team member consistently completes assignments on time but rarely shares progress updates with the rest of the team. This has caused coordination problems on several occasions. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Assign another team member to monitor the individual's work.
optionB: Discuss the importance of transparent communication with the team member and agree on an appropriate reporting approach.
optionC: Escalate the issue to the functional manager immediately.
optionD: Reduce the team member's responsibilities to minimize project risk.
explanation: The project manager should address communication issues directly with the team member, emphasizing collaboration and transparency before considering escalation.

question: Which TWO components are part of the Project Management Plan? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Schedule Management Plan
optionB: Risk Management Plan
optionC: Business Case
optionD: Project Charter
explanation: The Project Management Plan consists of subsidiary management plans, including the Schedule Management Plan and Risk Management Plan. The Business Case and Project Charter are project documents, not components of the Project Management Plan.

question: A project delivering a customer relationship management (CRM) system is almost complete when a new corporate strategy emphasizes artificial intelligence capabilities. Executives ask whether the current solution should be modified before deployment. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Delay deployment until all requested AI features are developed.
optionB: Evaluate the impact of the new strategic direction on the project's expected benefits, scope and business case before recommending a course of action.
optionC: Implement the requested AI features immediately because they align with the new strategy.
optionD: Reject the request because the project is in its final phase.
explanation: Strategic changes should trigger an assessment of their impact on the project's expected benefits, objectives and business case before decisions are made regarding scope or delivery.

question: According to Scrum, who is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team?
optionA: Scrum Master
optionB: Development Team
optionC: Project Sponsor
optionD: Product Owner
explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing product value by managing and ordering the Product Backlog, ensuring that the Scrum Team works on the highest-value items first.

question: During execution, a project manager notices that several completed deliverables have not been formally accepted by the customer, even though they meet all documented requirements. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Proceed with the remaining work because acceptance can occur at project closure.
optionB: Work with the customer to perform the agreed validation and acceptance process for the completed deliverables.
optionC: Update the project schedule to show the deliverables as accepted.
optionD: Submit a change request to remove the acceptance requirement.
explanation: Completing a deliverable is different from obtaining formal acceptance. The project manager should ensure that the agreed validation and acceptance process is followed before considering the deliverable accepted.

question: Which conflict resolution technique is generally considered the MOST effective because it addresses the root cause of the conflict while seeking a win-win solution?
optionA: Withdraw/Avoid
optionB: Collaborate/Problem Solve
optionC: Force/Direct
optionD: Smooth/Accommodate
explanation: Collaborate/Problem Solve is generally the preferred conflict resolution technique because it addresses the underlying cause of the conflict and seeks a solution acceptable to all parties.

question: A company announces a sustainability initiative that will affect several ongoing projects. Which TWO actions should the project manager take? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Assess how the new sustainability objectives affect the project's scope, benefits and success criteria.
optionB: Meet with the sponsor and key stakeholders to determine whether project plans should be updated.
optionC: Continue the project exactly as planned because environmental initiatives are organizational responsibilities.
optionD: Suspend the project until new organizational standards are finalized.
explanation: Strategic organizational initiatives such as sustainability programs may affect project objectives, expected benefits and success criteria. The project manager should evaluate the impact and work with stakeholders to determine appropriate changes.

question: Which schedule management technique focuses on progressively elaborating near-term work while planning future work at a higher level until more information becomes available?
optionA: Crashing
optionB: Fast Tracking
optionC: Rolling Wave Planning
optionD: Resource Leveling
explanation: Rolling Wave Planning is a form of progressive elaboration in which near-term work is planned in detail while future work remains at a higher level until sufficient information is available.

question: A project manager notices that a stakeholder frequently interrupts meetings and dismisses ideas from other participants. Team members have become reluctant to contribute during discussions. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Ask the stakeholder to leave future meetings.
optionB: Speak privately with the stakeholder to explain the impact of the behavior and reinforce the expected meeting norms.
optionC: Allow the behavior because the stakeholder has significant organizational influence.
optionD: Limit all future meetings to written status updates.
explanation: The project manager should address disruptive behavior directly and respectfully while reinforcing agreed meeting norms. Private coaching is typically more effective than public confrontation and helps preserve productive stakeholder relationships.

question: Which project artifact is primarily used to map project stakeholders according to their level of power and interest?
optionA: Stakeholder Engagement Assessment Matrix
optionB: Power/Interest Grid
optionC: Communications Management Plan
optionD: Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM)
explanation: The Power/Interest Grid is a stakeholder analysis tool used to classify stakeholders based on their authority and level of interest in the project. This helps the project manager determine the most appropriate engagement strategy.

question: A senior stakeholder regularly contacts individual developers to request status updates instead of following the agreed communication process. Team members are spending increasing amounts of time answering duplicate questions. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Ask the developers to ignore all future requests from the stakeholder.
optionB: Meet with the stakeholder to understand the information needs and reinforce the agreed communication approach while ensuring those needs are met.
optionC: Escalate the stakeholder's behavior to the project sponsor immediately.
optionD: Require developers to copy the project manager on every response.
explanation: The project manager should first understand why the stakeholder is bypassing the communication process and address the underlying need. Reinforcing the agreed communication approach while ensuring stakeholders receive timely information promotes collaboration and reduces unnecessary interruptions.

question: Which TWO documents are updated most frequently as part of ongoing risk management? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Risk Register
optionB: Risk Report
optionC: Project Charter
optionD: Business Case
explanation: The Risk Register contains detailed information about individual risks, owners and responses, while the Risk Report provides an overall view of project risk exposure and trends. Both are updated throughout the project as new information becomes available.

question: A project is developing a mobile payment platform when the government announces new regulations requiring stronger customer authentication before the planned release date. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Implement the new security requirements immediately without further analysis.
optionB: Assess the impact of the regulatory changes on project scope, schedule, cost, risks and expected benefits before determining the appropriate response.
optionC: Delay the project until the regulations become mandatory.
optionD: Ignore the announcement because the requirements are outside the project's approved scope.
explanation: Regulatory changes should first be evaluated to determine their impact on project objectives and compliance obligations. Decisions regarding scope or schedule changes should be based on that assessment.

question: Which document defines the roles, responsibilities and reporting relationships for project resources?
optionA: Resource Management Plan
optionB: Quality Management Plan
optionC: Procurement Management Plan
optionD: Benefits Management Plan
explanation: The Resource Management Plan describes how project resources will be acquired, managed and released. It also defines roles, responsibilities, reporting relationships and team management approaches.

question: A project manager discovers that several team members are using outdated versions of project documents because they saved local copies months earlier. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Require every team member to recreate their work using the outdated documents.
optionB: Restore the use of the controlled document repository, communicate the latest approved versions and assess whether any completed work is affected.
optionC: Create a new document repository for future projects.
optionD: Ignore the issue because the project is still on schedule.
explanation: Configuration management requires team members to use the latest approved documents. The project manager should restore document control, communicate the correct versions and evaluate any impact on completed work.

question: Which communication model element represents the method used to transmit a message from the sender to the receiver?
optionA: Feedback
optionB: Medium
optionC: Noise
optionD: Encoding
explanation: The medium is the channel through which a message is transmitted, such as a face-to-face conversation, phone call, email or video conference. Selecting the appropriate medium improves communication effectiveness.

question: A project manager identifies that several project assumptions have become invalid due to changes in market conditions. Which TWO actions should the project manager take? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Review the impact of the invalid assumptions on project risks, plans and objectives.
optionB: Update the Assumption Log and related project documents as appropriate.
optionC: Delete the assumptions without documenting the reason for the change.
optionD: Wait until project closure to review the affected assumptions.
explanation: Assumptions should be monitored throughout the project. When assumptions become invalid, the project manager should assess their impact and update project documentation to reflect the new situation.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of the Benefits Management Plan after the project has delivered its outputs?
optionA: To authorize project closure.
optionB: To define how expected benefits will be measured, transitioned and sustained over time.
optionC: To establish the project's procurement strategy.
optionD: To identify project stakeholders.
explanation: Many project benefits are realized after project completion. The Benefits Management Plan defines how those benefits will be measured, transitioned to operations and sustained to ensure the organization receives the intended value.

question: A project manager notices that discussions during team meetings are dominated by the same few individuals, while other team members remain silent despite having relevant expertise. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Assign speaking time to each participant and facilitate discussions to encourage balanced participation.
optionB: Allow the most experienced team members to continue leading all discussions.
optionC: Replace the quieter team members with more outspoken individuals.
optionD: Collect all technical decisions through email instead of holding meetings.
explanation: Effective facilitation encourages balanced participation and psychological safety, allowing the project manager to benefit from the knowledge and experience of the entire team rather than only the most vocal members.

question: Which project artifact provides a detailed description of each work package contained in the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?
optionA: Activity List
optionB: WBS Dictionary
optionC: Scope Baseline
optionD: Requirements Documentation
explanation: The WBS Dictionary provides detailed information about each work package in the WBS, including descriptions, assumptions, constraints, responsible organizations and acceptance criteria.

question: A newly assigned project sponsor frequently requests detailed technical explanations during steering committee meetings, causing discussions to run out of time before strategic decisions can be made. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Continue providing all requested technical details during the meetings.
optionB: Meet with the sponsor to understand the information needs and agree on a reporting approach that separates strategic decisions from technical details.
optionC: Ask the technical lead to replace the project manager in future steering committee meetings.
optionD: Remove technical topics from future meeting agendas.
explanation: The project manager should tailor communications to stakeholder needs while ensuring governance meetings remain focused on their intended purpose. Understanding the sponsor's information needs is the first step.

question: Which TWO techniques are commonly used to identify project risks? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Brainstorming
optionB: Expert Judgment
optionC: Schedule Crashing
optionD: Resource Leveling
explanation: Brainstorming and Expert Judgment are widely used during risk identification to uncover threats and opportunities. Schedule Crashing and Resource Leveling are schedule management techniques rather than risk identification techniques.

question: A project to implement an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system is entering the deployment phase when the organization announces a major restructuring that will change business processes in several departments. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Proceed with deployment because the project is nearly complete.
optionB: Assess the impact of the organizational changes on project objectives, benefits, stakeholders and deployment plans before recommending any adjustments.
optionC: Delay deployment indefinitely until the restructuring is finished.
optionD: Cancel the deployment because organizational priorities have changed.
explanation: Significant organizational changes can affect stakeholder needs, expected benefits and deployment activities. The project manager should first assess the impact before recommending changes to the project.

question: In Scrum, what is the PRIMARY purpose of the Daily Scrum?
optionA: To report progress to the Product Owner.
optionB: To inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan for the next 24 hours.
optionC: To demonstrate completed work to stakeholders.
optionD: To estimate the Product Backlog items for the next Sprint.
explanation: The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan for the next day. Its purpose is to improve coordination and increase the likelihood of achieving the Sprint Goal.

question: During project execution, a team member proposes a more efficient way to complete a deliverable that will reduce costs without affecting scope or quality. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Implement the new approach immediately because it reduces project costs.
optionB: Evaluate the proposal to determine its impact on project baselines, risks and constraints before deciding whether a change is required.
optionC: Reject the proposal because the project management plan has already been approved.
optionD: Ask the team member to wait until the project is closed before suggesting improvements.
explanation: The project manager should first assess the proposed improvement and determine whether it affects approved baselines or requires formal change control. Beneficial improvements should be evaluated rather than automatically accepted or rejected.

question: Which document or artifact is MOST useful for clarifying who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for project activities?
optionA: Stakeholder Register
optionB: RACI Matrix
optionC: Resource Calendar
optionD: Communications Management Plan
explanation: A RACI Matrix is a type of Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) that clarifies roles by identifying who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each activity or deliverable.

question: Which TWO statements about the Critical Path are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Activities on the critical path have the least scheduling flexibility.
optionB: A delay to a critical path activity may delay the project's completion date.
optionC: Critical path activities always require the largest project budget.
optionD: The critical path never changes during project execution.
explanation: The critical path is the longest path through the schedule network and determines the earliest possible project completion date. Activities on this path have little or no float, and delays to them can delay the overall project. The critical path can change as the project progresses.

question: A project is delivering a new warehouse management system. Shortly before implementation, the customer announces the acquisition of another company that will require integration with an additional logistics platform. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Add the integration work to the current release immediately.
optionB: Assess the impact of the acquisition on project objectives, scope, schedule, benefits and stakeholders before recommending a course of action.
optionC: Delay the implementation until all integration work has been completed.
optionD: Reject the request because the acquisition occurred after planning was completed.
explanation: Organizational acquisitions often affect project scope, stakeholders and expected benefits. The project manager should first evaluate the impact before recommending changes through the appropriate governance process.

question: According to the Scrum Guide, who is responsible for managing the Sprint Backlog during a Sprint?
optionA: Product Owner
optionB: Scrum Master
optionC: Developers
optionD: Project Manager
explanation: The Developers are responsible for creating and managing the Sprint Backlog. They adapt it as needed throughout the Sprint to achieve the Sprint Goal, while the Product Owner manages the Product Backlog.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a Project Management Information System (PMIS)?
optionA: To replace the project manager in making project decisions.
optionB: To support the collection, integration, analysis and distribution of project information.
optionC: To approve all project change requests automatically.
optionD: To store only financial information related to the project.
explanation: A Project Management Information System (PMIS) supports project planning, execution, monitoring and reporting by collecting, integrating and distributing project information. It assists decision-making but does not replace the project manager.

question: A newly appointed product owner has an excellent understanding of the business but struggles to prioritize the Product Backlog because every stakeholder claims their request is the highest priority. What should the Scrum Master do FIRST?
optionA: Prioritize the backlog on behalf of the Product Owner.
optionB: Coach the Product Owner on value-based prioritization techniques and facilitate discussions with stakeholders to clarify business value.
optionC: Ask the development team to rank the backlog items by implementation effort.
optionD: Request that the sponsor prioritize all backlog items.
explanation: The Scrum Master coaches the Product Owner and facilitates collaboration. The Product Owner remains accountable for backlog ordering, which should be based on value rather than stakeholder influence.

question: Which TWO Earned Value Management (EVM) metrics indicate project performance? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Schedule Performance Index (SPI)
optionB: Cost Performance Index (CPI)
optionC: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)
optionD: Product Backlog
explanation: SPI measures schedule efficiency, while CPI measures cost efficiency. Both are core Earned Value Management performance indicators used to evaluate project performance.

question: A project to implement an electronic procurement system is underway when the organization's procurement policy is revised to require additional supplier due diligence. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Continue using the existing procurement process because contracts have already been planned.
optionB: Assess the impact of the new procurement policy on the project and update the procurement approach as necessary through the appropriate governance process.
optionC: Cancel all procurement activities until the policy is finalized.
optionD: Delegate responsibility for the policy change entirely to the procurement department.
explanation: Changes to organizational policies should be assessed for their impact on the project. The project manager should evaluate the effect on procurement activities and update project plans through the appropriate governance process.

question: According to PMI, what is the PRIMARY objective of stakeholder engagement?
optionA: To ensure every stakeholder approves every project decision.
optionB: To build productive relationships that support successful project outcomes.
optionC: To reduce the number of stakeholders participating in the project.
optionD: To communicate project status only at major milestones.
explanation: Stakeholder engagement focuses on building and maintaining productive relationships, understanding stakeholder needs and expectations, and encouraging appropriate involvement to improve the likelihood of project success.

question: A project manager learns that a key supplier will be unable to deliver a critical component on the agreed date due to a natural disaster. The delay could affect the project's critical path. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Submit a claim against the supplier for breach of contract.
optionB: Assess the impact on the project schedule, identify response options and communicate the risk to relevant stakeholders.
optionC: Immediately replace the supplier with another vendor.
optionD: Delay all remaining project activities until the component is delivered.
explanation: When a significant risk materializes, the project manager should first assess its impact, evaluate response options and communicate appropriately. Decisions such as changing suppliers should be based on that assessment.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a team charter?
optionA: To define the project's budget baseline.
optionB: To establish team values, working agreements and expected behaviors.
optionC: To document the project's procurement strategy.
optionD: To identify project risks and response plans.
explanation: A team charter establishes shared expectations regarding values, communication, decision-making, conflict management and team norms. It helps improve collaboration and team performance.

question: Which TWO actions are typically performed during the Control Quality process? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Inspect completed deliverables.
optionB: Verify that deliverables comply with quality requirements.
optionC: Approve the project charter.
optionD: Develop the project schedule baseline.
explanation: Control Quality focuses on inspecting deliverables and verifying that they meet the defined quality requirements before they are presented for formal acceptance.

question: Midway through a digital transformation project, executive leadership changes the organization's strategic priorities. Some planned features no longer support the new business objectives. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Continue delivering all approved features because they are included in the scope baseline.
optionB: Evaluate how the strategic changes affect the project's objectives, expected benefits and scope before recommending any changes.
optionC: Remove the affected features from the project without stakeholder approval.
optionD: Stop all project work until a new sponsor is appointed.
explanation: Projects should remain aligned with organizational strategy. The project manager should first assess the impact of strategic changes and then follow the appropriate governance and change management processes.

question: In an Agile environment, what is the PRIMARY benefit of using cross-functional teams?
optionA: They eliminate the need for project planning.
optionB: They enable the team to deliver valuable increments with minimal dependencies on external groups.
optionC: They ensure every team member performs the same tasks.
optionD: They reduce the number of stakeholders involved in product development.
explanation: Cross-functional teams possess the diverse skills needed to deliver a product increment independently, reducing handoffs, external dependencies and delays while increasing adaptability.

question: During project execution, the customer requests a feature that would significantly increase the product's value. The technical team confirms the feature is feasible but estimates it will extend the project by two weeks. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Approve the feature because it provides additional customer value.
optionB: Reject the request because the scope baseline has already been approved.
optionC: Evaluate the impact of the requested change on scope, schedule, cost, risks and benefits before initiating the appropriate change process.
optionD: Ask the team to work overtime so the schedule is not affected.
explanation: Any requested change should first be analyzed to understand its impact on the project. The project manager should evaluate the implications and follow the organization's integrated change control process before making a decision.

question: Which leadership style focuses on empowering team members, removing impediments and helping others succeed rather than directing their work?
optionA: Transactional Leadership
optionB: Servant Leadership
optionC: Autocratic Leadership
optionD: Laissez-faire Leadership
explanation: Servant Leadership emphasizes serving the team, fostering collaboration, coaching individuals and removing obstacles so the team can perform at its highest level. It is widely associated with Agile approaches.

question: Which TWO statements about the Perform Integrated Change Control process are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Every change request should be evaluated before being approved, rejected or deferred.
optionB: Approved changes should be incorporated into the relevant project documents and baselines.
optionC: Only the project sponsor may submit change requests.
optionD: Changes may be implemented before evaluation if they appear to improve project performance.
explanation: Integrated Change Control ensures that all change requests are formally reviewed and their impacts assessed before a decision is made. Once approved, the corresponding project documents, plans and baselines are updated as appropriate.

question: A government agency issues new data privacy regulations that will become effective before the planned deployment of your project. The project is currently on schedule, but compliance has not been considered. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Deploy the solution as planned and address compliance after implementation.
optionB: Assess the impact of the new regulations on project requirements, risks, scope and delivery strategy, then engage the appropriate stakeholders.
optionC: Immediately suspend the project until the regulations are fully understood.
optionD: Ignore the regulations because they were published after the project was approved.
explanation: Regulatory changes may affect project scope, compliance obligations and expected benefits. The project manager should first assess the impact and engage the appropriate stakeholders before determining the required actions.

question: According to the Tuckman model of team development, during which stage do team members establish trust, resolve differences and begin working more collaboratively?
optionA: Forming
optionB: Storming
optionC: Norming
optionD: Performing
explanation: During the Norming stage, team members develop stronger relationships, establish shared norms, resolve many earlier conflicts and begin collaborating more effectively, preparing the team for high performance.

question: During execution, a key stakeholder requests a progress report that includes information not defined in the Communications Management Plan. Providing the report will require significant effort from the project team. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Decline the request because it is not included in the Communications Management Plan.
optionB: Evaluate the stakeholder's information needs and determine whether the communication approach should be updated.
optionC: Instruct the team to prepare the report immediately to satisfy the stakeholder.
optionD: Escalate the request to the sponsor for approval.
explanation: The project manager should first understand the stakeholder's information needs and determine whether the communication strategy remains appropriate. If necessary, communication plans should be updated through the appropriate project management processes.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of emotional intelligence for a project manager?
optionA: To ensure all stakeholders agree with every project decision.
optionB: To recognize, understand and manage emotions in oneself and others to improve relationships and project outcomes.
optionC: To evaluate the technical competence of project team members.
optionD: To reduce the need for formal communication.
explanation: Emotional intelligence enables project managers to recognize and manage emotions, build trust, resolve conflicts effectively and foster productive relationships with stakeholders and team members.

question: Which TWO statements about the Validate Scope process are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Its primary objective is to obtain formal acceptance of completed deliverables.
optionB: It is typically performed with the customer or sponsor.
optionC: It focuses on identifying process improvements for future projects.
optionD: It verifies that project expenditures remain within the approved budget.
explanation: Validate Scope is the process of formalizing acceptance of completed deliverables. It is typically conducted with the customer or sponsor to ensure the deliverables satisfy the documented acceptance criteria.

question: A merger between two organizations is approved while your project is integrating their customer service platforms. Each organization has different business processes and reporting requirements. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Continue following the original project plan because it was already approved.
optionB: Assess the impact of the merger on project objectives, stakeholders, requirements and expected benefits before recommending changes.
optionC: Pause the project until all business processes have been standardized.
optionD: Ask each department to implement its own version of the solution.
explanation: Major organizational changes can significantly affect project objectives, stakeholders and business value. The project manager should first perform an impact assessment before initiating changes through the appropriate governance process.

question: Which Agile principle encourages teams to regularly reflect on how to become more effective and adjust their behavior accordingly?
optionA: Working software is the primary measure of progress.
optionB: At regular intervals, the team reflects on how to become more effective, then tunes and adjusts its behavior accordingly.
optionC: Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project.
optionD: Welcome changing requirements, even late in development.
explanation: One of the Agile Manifesto principles emphasizes continuous improvement through regular team reflection, typically performed during retrospectives, where the team identifies ways to improve future performance.

question: Halfway through execution, the project manager discovers that several approved change requests have not been incorporated into the latest project schedule. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Update the project schedule to reflect the approved changes and evaluate any resulting impacts on the project baselines.
optionB: Ignore the discrepancy because the changes have already been approved.
optionC: Submit new change requests for each missing update.
optionD: Wait until the next reporting cycle before updating the schedule.
explanation: Approved changes must be incorporated into the appropriate project management plan components and baselines. The project manager should update the schedule promptly and assess any resulting impacts on the project's objectives.

question: A highly skilled team member consistently delivers excellent work but refuses to share knowledge with the rest of the team, creating a dependency that threatens the project schedule if that person becomes unavailable. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Reassign the team member to another project.
optionB: Meet privately with the team member to understand the reasons for the behavior and encourage knowledge sharing through collaborative practices.
optionC: Escalate the issue to functional management immediately.
optionD: Document the risk and take no further action unless the team member resigns.
explanation: The project manager should first address the issue directly by understanding the underlying cause and promoting collaboration. Knowledge sharing reduces project risk, improves team capability and minimizes dependency on a single individual.

question: Which TWO statements about the Scope Baseline are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: It consists of the Project Scope Statement, the WBS and the WBS Dictionary.
optionB: It serves as the basis for measuring and controlling scope performance.
optionC: It is updated every time a team member suggests an improvement.
optionD: It replaces the Requirements Documentation after project planning.
explanation: The Scope Baseline is composed of the approved Project Scope Statement, WBS and WBS Dictionary. It is used to measure project performance and evaluate proposed scope changes through integrated change control.

question: A project is implementing a cloud-based solution when the organization's cybersecurity department introduces a mandatory security review before any production deployment. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Deploy the solution as scheduled and complete the review afterward.
optionB: Assess the impact of the new governance requirement on the project schedule, risks and deployment plan, then coordinate with the appropriate stakeholders.
optionC: Request an exemption because the project is nearing completion.
optionD: Delay the project indefinitely until the cybersecurity policy is revised.
explanation: New governance requirements should first be evaluated for their impact on the project. The project manager should assess schedule, risk and compliance implications before determining the appropriate response.

question: Which communication method is generally MOST appropriate when discussing a sensitive issue that requires immediate feedback and clarification?
optionA: Email
optionB: Project dashboard
optionC: Face-to-face meeting or video conference
optionD: Weekly status report
explanation: Sensitive topics are best addressed through interactive communication methods such as face-to-face meetings or video conferences because they enable immediate feedback, clarification and observation of nonverbal cues.

question: During project monitoring, the project manager discovers that actual costs are below budget, but Earned Value analysis shows the project is behind schedule. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Celebrate the cost savings because the project is under budget.
optionB: Analyze the root cause of the schedule variance and evaluate corrective actions before making adjustments.
optionC: Increase project spending immediately to recover the schedule.
optionD: Request additional funding from the sponsor.
explanation: Earned Value metrics should be analyzed to understand the cause of variances before corrective actions are taken. Being under budget does not necessarily indicate good project performance if schedule objectives are at risk.

question: According to PMI, what is the PRIMARY benefit of active listening?
optionA: It reduces the need for project documentation.
optionB: It improves understanding, builds trust and reduces misunderstandings.
optionC: It allows the project manager to control every conversation.
optionD: It eliminates conflicts among stakeholders.
explanation: Active listening involves paying full attention, asking clarifying questions and confirming understanding. It strengthens relationships, improves communication and helps prevent misunderstandings.

question: During execution, a quality inspection reveals that a recently completed deliverable does not meet an approved acceptance criterion. The customer has not yet reviewed the deliverable. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Submit the deliverable to the customer and explain the issue afterward.
optionB: Correct the nonconformance through the appropriate quality process before requesting formal acceptance.
optionC: Ask the customer to waive the acceptance criterion.
optionD: Remove the acceptance criterion from the project scope.
explanation: Control Quality should identify and correct defects before deliverables are presented for Validate Scope. Deliverables should meet approved quality and acceptance criteria before formal customer acceptance is requested.

question: Which TWO statements about the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: It links requirements to project objectives, deliverables and verification activities.
optionB: It helps ensure each approved requirement delivers business value and is tested.
optionC: It replaces the Scope Baseline after project planning.
optionD: It is used only in predictive projects.
explanation: The Requirements Traceability Matrix links requirements from their origin through implementation and verification. It helps ensure that every approved requirement supports business value and is validated appropriately.

question: A project is developing a customer portal when the marketing department identifies a new market opportunity that could significantly increase future revenue but would require additional functionality. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Approve the additional functionality because it increases business value.
optionB: Assess the impact of the opportunity on the project's business case, scope, schedule, costs and expected benefits before recommending a decision.
optionC: Reject the proposal because development has already started.
optionD: Delay the project until a new business case is approved.
explanation: Projects should remain aligned with organizational strategy and business value. The project manager should first evaluate the impact of the opportunity before recommending changes through the appropriate governance process.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a Sprint Retrospective in Scrum?
optionA: To demonstrate the completed Increment to stakeholders.
optionB: To inspect how the team worked during the Sprint and identify improvements for future Sprints.
optionC: To prioritize the Product Backlog.
optionD: To estimate the effort for the next Sprint.
explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity for the Scrum Team to inspect its processes, collaboration and tools, then identify actionable improvements to increase effectiveness in future Sprints.

question: During project execution, a stakeholder reports that a completed deliverable does not satisfy a requirement. The project manager verifies that the requirement was omitted from the design documents but is included in the approved Requirements Documentation. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Reject the stakeholder's concern because the design documents were approved.
optionB: Analyze the impact of the omission, determine why it occurred and initiate the appropriate change or corrective action process.
optionC: Immediately instruct the team to implement the missing requirement without further evaluation.
optionD: Remove the requirement from the Requirements Documentation.
explanation: The project manager should first determine the root cause and assess the impact of the omission. Since the requirement is approved, appropriate corrective actions and change control processes should be followed before implementation.

question: Which motivation theory proposes that people are motivated by the need for Achievement, Affiliation and Power?
optionA: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
optionB: Herzberg's Motivation-Hygiene Theory
optionC: McClelland's Theory of Needs
optionD: McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y
explanation: McClelland's Theory of Needs identifies three dominant motivators: Achievement, Affiliation and Power. Understanding these needs helps project managers tailor leadership and motivation approaches.

question: Which TWO statements about the Project Schedule are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: It contains the planned start and finish dates for project activities and milestones.
optionB: It is used to monitor and control schedule performance throughout the project.
optionC: It permanently replaces the Schedule Baseline after project execution begins.
optionD: It can never be updated after it has been approved.
explanation: The Project Schedule includes planned activity and milestone dates and is used throughout execution to monitor schedule performance. Approved schedule changes are reflected through formal change control, meaning the schedule is not static.

question: A project supporting a corporate sustainability initiative identifies an opportunity to reduce operating costs while also decreasing environmental impact. Implementing the improvement will require changes to the approved scope. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Approve the improvement because it increases organizational value.
optionB: Assess the impact on the business case, scope, schedule, cost, risks and expected benefits before submitting the proposal through the change control process.
optionC: Reject the proposal because sustainability improvements were not included in the original scope.
optionD: Implement the change during the next project phase without notifying stakeholders.
explanation: Even beneficial changes should be evaluated for their impact on the project and processed through the organization's change control procedures before implementation.

question: A distributed Agile team has experienced a noticeable decline in participation during Sprint Planning meetings. Several remote team members rarely contribute, and important risks are being identified late in the Sprint. What should the Scrum Master do FIRST?
optionA: Assign backlog items to team members before the meeting.
optionB: Facilitate an open discussion with the team to understand the causes of low participation and adjust meeting practices to encourage engagement.
optionC: Require every team member to keep their camera on throughout the meeting.
optionD: Reduce the duration of Sprint Planning to avoid unnecessary discussions.
explanation: The Scrum Master should first understand the underlying causes of low engagement and facilitate improvements to team collaboration. Addressing the root cause promotes transparency, participation and better Sprint Planning outcomes.

question: Which project document identifies individual project risks, their causes, potential responses, owners and current status?
optionA: Risk Report
optionB: Issue Log
optionC: Risk Register
optionD: Lessons Learned Register
explanation: The Risk Register contains detailed information about identified risks, including descriptions, causes, probability, impact, owners, response strategies and current status. It is updated throughout the project.

question: A project manager notices increasing tension between the development team and the quality assurance team. Misunderstandings are causing delays and reducing trust. Which TWO actions should the project manager take? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Facilitate a collaborative discussion to identify the root causes of the conflict and agree on shared working practices.
optionB: Review and reinforce the team's working agreements and communication expectations.
optionC: Separate the two teams completely to minimize future interaction.
optionD: Escalate the disagreement to senior management without attempting resolution.
explanation: The project manager should encourage collaboration by addressing the underlying causes of conflict and reinforcing agreed team norms. Escalation should generally occur only after appropriate conflict resolution efforts have been attempted.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a business case throughout a project's life cycle?
optionA: To define detailed technical specifications for the solution.
optionB: To justify the project's continued existence by demonstrating that expected business value outweighs the investment.
optionC: To assign responsibilities to project team members.
optionD: To establish the project's communication channels.
explanation: The business case explains why the project should be undertaken and provides the business justification. It may be reviewed throughout the project to ensure the expected benefits continue to support the investment.

question: While reviewing project performance, the project manager discovers that a work package has been completed without meeting the agreed Definition of Done. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Accept the work because the functionality has been delivered.
optionB: Work with the team to complete the missing acceptance criteria before considering the work complete.
optionC: Ask the customer to waive the Definition of Done.
optionD: Remove the incomplete tasks from the Sprint Backlog.
explanation: The Definition of Done establishes the quality standards required before work is considered complete. If those criteria are not satisfied, the work should not be treated as complete until the remaining requirements are fulfilled.

question: Which leadership behavior is MOST effective for developing a high-performing project team over time?
optionA: Making all significant decisions without team involvement.
optionB: Providing coaching, constructive feedback and opportunities for continuous learning.
optionC: Assigning only routine work to less experienced team members.
optionD: Evaluating team members exclusively based on schedule performance.
explanation: High-performing teams are developed through coaching, feedback, mentoring and continuous learning. These practices improve competence, engagement, collaboration and long-term team performance.

question: Which estimate is generally considered the MOST accurate because it is based on detailed information about individual work packages?
optionA: Analogous Estimating
optionB: Parametric Estimating
optionC: Bottom-Up Estimating
optionD: Three-Point Estimating
explanation: Bottom-Up Estimating calculates estimates at the lowest level of the WBS and aggregates them to produce the overall project estimate. Although time-consuming, it is generally the most accurate estimating technique.

question: A new team member repeatedly misses important project information because meetings are scheduled outside the individual's normal working hours in another time zone. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Require the team member to attend every meeting regardless of local working hours.
optionB: Review the team's communication approach and adjust meeting schedules or communication methods to support effective participation by all team members.
optionC: Exclude the team member from meetings and send written summaries.
optionD: Ask the functional manager to replace the team member with someone in the same time zone.
explanation: The project manager should tailor communications to the needs of the team. For distributed teams, meeting schedules and communication methods should promote inclusion and effective collaboration.

question: Which TWO statements about procurement contracts are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: A Fixed-Price contract places most cost risk on the seller.
optionB: A Cost-Reimbursable contract generally places more cost risk on the buyer.
optionC: A Time and Materials contract always transfers all risk to the seller.
optionD: Contract type has no influence on how project risks are allocated.
explanation: Fixed-Price contracts typically shift cost risk to the seller, while Cost-Reimbursable contracts place more cost risk on the buyer. Time and Materials contracts allocate risk between both parties depending on their terms.

question: During execution, the organization's executive committee approves a new strategic initiative that competes for the same specialized resources assigned to your project. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Refuse to release any resources because the project has already started.
optionB: Assess the impact of the resource changes on project objectives, schedule, risks and expected benefits, then discuss options with the sponsor and relevant stakeholders.
optionC: Reduce the project scope without consulting stakeholders.
optionD: Immediately request additional external resources regardless of cost.
explanation: Strategic organizational changes may require reprioritization of resources. The project manager should first assess the impact and collaborate with governance stakeholders before determining the appropriate response.

question: What is the PRIMARY objective of a stakeholder engagement assessment matrix?
optionA: To estimate stakeholder influence on the project budget.
optionB: To compare current and desired stakeholder engagement levels and identify where engagement strategies are needed.
optionC: To assign project resources to stakeholder requests.
optionD: To prioritize project risks according to stakeholder preferences.
explanation: A Stakeholder Engagement Assessment Matrix compares current and desired engagement levels for each stakeholder, helping the project manager identify gaps and develop appropriate engagement strategies.

question: A project manager discovers that several approved project documents contain conflicting information about a key deliverable. Team members are unsure which version to follow. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Allow each team to use the version they believe is correct.
optionB: Identify the approved baseline, resolve the inconsistency through configuration management and communicate the correct information to the team.
optionC: Delay all work on the deliverable until the next steering committee meeting.
optionD: Ask the customer to choose which document should be followed.
explanation: Configuration management ensures that approved project information remains accurate and consistent. The project manager should identify the correct baseline, resolve discrepancies and communicate the approved information before work continues.

question: Which technique is MOST appropriate for reaching a group decision when all participants support the final outcome, even if it is not everyone's preferred option?
optionA: Majority
optionB: Plurality
optionC: Consensus
optionD: Autocratic Decision
explanation: Consensus is achieved when participants can support a decision that everyone is willing to accept, even if it is not each person's preferred choice. It generally promotes stronger commitment to implementation.

question: Which TWO statements about schedule float are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Total float is the amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project's planned completion date.
optionB: Activities on the critical path generally have zero or very little total float.
optionC: Free float always equals total float.
optionD: Float can only decrease as the project progresses.
explanation: Total float represents the scheduling flexibility available before affecting the project's completion date. Activities on the critical path typically have zero or near-zero total float. Free float and total float are different concepts, and float may increase or decrease as the schedule changes.

question: An organization acquires a competitor while your project is developing a customer relationship management platform. Leadership wants to incorporate customer data from the acquired company. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Approve the additional work because it increases business value.
optionB: Assess the impact of the acquisition on project scope, schedule, cost, risks, compliance requirements and expected benefits before recommending changes.
optionC: Reject the request because it was not included in the original charter.
optionD: Delay all project activities until the acquisition is fully completed.
explanation: Major organizational events such as acquisitions can significantly affect project objectives, stakeholders and business value. The project manager should first evaluate the impact before initiating formal change management.

question: In a servant leadership approach, which action BEST demonstrates the project manager's role?
optionA: Assigning tasks without team input to maximize efficiency.
optionB: Removing obstacles, coaching team members and enabling them to succeed.
optionC: Making all project decisions independently to reduce delays.
optionD: Evaluating team members primarily on individual productivity metrics.
explanation: Servant leaders focus on enabling the team's success by removing impediments, providing coaching, fostering collaboration and creating an environment where team members can perform at their best.

question: During project execution, a customer asks whether a recently approved change request has already been incorporated into the project plans. What should the project manager verify FIRST?
optionA: Whether the project budget has sufficient contingency reserves.
optionB: Whether the approved change has been implemented by updating the relevant project documents, baselines and work plans.
optionC: Whether the change request was submitted before the scheduled deadline.
optionD: Whether all stakeholders have verbally acknowledged the change.
explanation: Once a change request is approved, the project manager should ensure that all affected project documents, baselines and plans are updated before execution continues. Approval alone does not implement a change.

question: Which interpersonal skill helps a project manager understand the underlying interests behind stakeholder positions during negotiations?
optionA: Benchmarking
optionB: Active Listening
optionC: Parametric Estimating
optionD: Trend Analysis
explanation: Active listening enables the project manager to understand stakeholder concerns, motivations and interests, leading to more effective negotiations and stronger relationships.

question: Which TWO statements about configuration management are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: It helps maintain the integrity and consistency of project deliverables and documentation.
optionB: It ensures approved changes are properly identified, documented and tracked.
optionC: It eliminates the need for Integrated Change Control.
optionD: It applies only to software development projects.
explanation: Configuration management establishes and maintains the consistency of project artifacts and ensures approved changes are correctly identified, documented and controlled. It complements, rather than replaces, Integrated Change Control and is applicable across all project types.

question: A new environmental regulation requires additional testing before a product can be released. The project is nearing completion and the new testing was not included in the original scope. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Release the product as originally planned and complete the testing later.
optionB: Assess the impact of the regulatory requirement on scope, schedule, cost, risks and expected benefits before initiating the appropriate change process.
optionC: Ignore the regulation because it was introduced after project approval.
optionD: Cancel the project because compliance requirements have changed.
explanation: Regulatory changes should first be analyzed to understand their impact on the project. The project manager should then follow governance and change control processes to determine the appropriate course of action.

question: Which characteristic BEST describes a self-organizing Agile team?
optionA: The project manager assigns all tasks and priorities.
optionB: The team determines how to accomplish its work while remaining accountable for meeting agreed objectives.
optionC: Team members work independently with minimal collaboration.
optionD: Only the Scrum Master decides how work is distributed among team members.
explanation: Self-organizing teams decide how to perform their work, collaborate to achieve shared goals and take collective ownership of outcomes. Leadership provides direction and support rather than assigning detailed tasks.

question: A project manager discovers that several completed activities were marked as finished even though supporting documentation was never uploaded to the organization's repository. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Close the activities because the work has already been completed.
optionB: Verify the completion criteria, ensure the required documentation is uploaded and update the project records before considering the activities complete.
optionC: Delete the incomplete records and recreate them after project closure.
optionD: Ignore the missing documentation because it does not affect the final product.
explanation: Project work should only be considered complete when all defined completion criteria have been met, including required documentation. Accurate records support governance, audits and future lessons learned.

question: Which communication technique is MOST effective for confirming that a message has been correctly understood by the receiver?
optionA: Sending a follow-up email without requesting feedback.
optionB: Using active listening techniques such as paraphrasing and asking clarifying questions.
optionC: Providing more detailed technical documentation.
optionD: Increasing the frequency of project status reports.
explanation: Active listening includes paraphrasing, confirming understanding and asking clarifying questions. These techniques reduce misunderstandings and improve communication effectiveness.

question: Which TWO statements about lessons learned are correct? (Select TWO answers.)
optionA: Lessons learned should be captured throughout the project, not only at project closure.
optionB: The Lessons Learned Register helps improve future projects and organizational knowledge.
optionC: Lessons learned should only document project failures.
optionD: The Lessons Learned Register is created only after all project deliverables have been accepted.
explanation: PMI recommends capturing lessons learned continuously during the project. The Lessons Learned Register promotes organizational learning by documenting both successful practices and opportunities for improvement.

question: Halfway through a product development project, senior management announces a strategic partnership with another company that will require compatibility with the partner's platform. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Commit to the integration because it supports the organization's strategy.
optionB: Assess the impact of the partnership on project scope, schedule, cost, risks, stakeholders and expected benefits before recommending changes.
optionC: Reject the request because it was not included in the original scope.
optionD: Delay the project until the partner completes its own implementation.
explanation: Strategic partnerships can significantly affect project objectives and deliverables. The project manager should first perform an impact assessment before initiating the appropriate governance and change management processes.

question: According to the PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, which value requires project professionals to make decisions and act impartially and objectively?
optionA: Respect
optionB: Responsibility
optionC: Fairness
optionD: Honesty
explanation: Fairness requires PMI professionals to make decisions objectively, avoid favoritism and conflicts of interest, and treat all stakeholders equitably. It is one of the four fundamental values of the PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct.

question: During project execution, the project manager discovers that a vendor has delivered all contracted items on time, but several contractual acceptance documents have not been completed. What should the project manager do FIRST?
optionA: Approve the vendor's final payment because the deliverables have been received.
optionB: Verify the contract acceptance requirements, complete the necessary procurement verification activities and obtain the required approvals before closing the procurement.
optionC: Close the procurement because the physical work has been completed.
optionD: Ask the vendor to prepare the missing documents after the project has been closed.
explanation: Procurement closure requires verifying that all contractual obligations, including required documentation and formal acceptance, have been completed before final payment and contract closure.

question: A project manager wants to improve team performance by increasing psychological safety. Which action BEST supports this objective?
optionA: Reward only team members who consistently outperform others.
optionB: Encourage open discussion, welcome different viewpoints and treat mistakes as learning opportunities when appropriate.
optionC: Require all disagreements to be escalated immediately to senior management.
optionD: Avoid discussing project failures to maintain team morale.
explanation: Psychological safety enables team members to speak openly, ask questions, admit mistakes and share ideas without fear of embarrassment or retaliation. This environment fosters innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.
